text:
maria: putting up a short proposal for OTEL span names + semantic attrs for LLM requests. want to reduce ambiguity between API-level calls, routing decisions, and runtime kernel spans.

maria: high-level rules: use a stable span name for the API-level call (llm.request), and granular internal names for runtime ops (llm.runtime, llm.kv_cache, llm.batch). prefix all attrs with llm. where appropriate.

jonathan: quick q — why a single llm.request name vs including the route in the name (eg llm.request.generate)?

maria: good question. prefer to keep the span name stable so dashboards/alerts don't explode when routes change. route can be an attribute: llm.route = "/v1/generate" or llm.route = "chat". easier for queries and rollouts.

sam: +1 on attributes. also: avoid putting customer_id raw in attrs (privacy). we should store hashed_customer_id or map id externally.

kai: agree on hashing. also, careful with model version attr cardinality — model.name is fine, model.version only when troubleshooting (sampling). otherwise it creates high-cardinality.

maria: noted. propose these attributes (names are exact strings we should use):

```
span.name = "llm.request"  # top-level, API-facing
attributes:
  "service.name": "redwood-inference"
  "llm.model": "gpt-4o-mini"
  "llm.model_version": "2026-03-01"    # optional, sampled for debug traces
  "llm.source": "hosted|dedicated|private"
  "llm.route": "/v1/chat"
  "llm.routing.policy": "latency-first|cost-first|region-pref"
  "llm.tokens.prompt": 120
  "llm.tokens.completion": 45
  "llm.tokens.total": 165
  "llm.cache.hit": true
  "llm.cache.strategy": "prefix_kv"
  "llm.batch.size": 4
  "llm.quantized": false
  "llm.latency_ms": 134.2
  "http.status_code": 200
  "telemetry.sampling.priority": 1  # 1=keep for retention/exporter decisions
```

jonathan: that looks solid. small nit: attribute names use dots and underscores mixed. OTEL doesn't forbid, but we should standardize. i'd prefer dot-prefix for domain (llm.model) and snake for subkeys (llm.model_version) — as you wrote.

sam: question about cache attributes — do we want to include cache.key? that could be PII/high-cardinality. i think we should only include cache.hit (bool) and cache.type.

maria: agree. no raw keys or prompts in attributes. prompts must never be in span attrs. store prompt fingerprints/hashes if needed.

kai: about exporters & retention: telemetry team wants a small set of hot traces with full attributes for ops, rest sampled with minimal attrs. propose: sampling decision attribute (telemetry.sampling.priority) + telemetry.export.set = [hot, analytics] so we can route.

telemetry-bot: deploy-check: new attribute names validated against policy v2? false

maria: good point — i'll run a lint against our attribute whitelist. plan: default exporter = metrics + traces (low-card attrs), hot traces when sampling.priority >= 1 and llm.cache.hit=false and latency_ms > 500 or http.status_code >= 500.

jonathan: we should also tag span with deployment scope: llm_env=prod/stage and infra_node vs dedicated_pool id (low-card).

sam: and add llm.deployment_type=hosted|dedicated|private as you had. that helps in console dashboards for per-customer routing.

maria: implementation notes for SDK/runtime teams:
- root span emitted at API gateway with span.name = "llm.request" and attributes listed above
- runtime creates child spans for routing decision: span.name = "llm.routing" attrs: llm.routing.policy, llm.route_candidate, llm.fallback_used (bool)
- runtime kernel spans: "llm.runtime" -> include llm.kv_cache.* child spans with only llm.cache.hit and llm.cache.strategy
- do NOT include prompt or output texts in any attribute

maria: sample query examples for dashboards:
```
count(span) by llm.model where span.name = "llm.request" and llm.source = "hosted"
avg(llm.latency_ms) by llm.model, llm.route
```

kai: sounds good. last UX ask: on the console, when we show a trace link from the dashboard, only surface model + route + tokens + cache.hit unless user clicks expand to see model_version & customer hash. keeps initial UI readable.

maria: agreed. i'll PR a spec doc with exact attr list and a small lint rule that fails build if someone emits an attr not on the whitelist.

jonathan: thanks — can you include fallback examples for dedicated/private where we might want extra attrs (infra.node_id) but gated behind sampling?

maria: yes — will include conditional attrs and sampling rules. planning to draft PR today.

sam: :thumbsup:

kai: thanks, will review the PR.

telemetry-bot: reminder: telemetry design review meeting weds 10am. RSVP if you want to argue about dots vs underscores :)
